chunks: From him, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Abu Basir, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both)

In the case of a man who married his slave woman to a free man for four hundred dirhams, so he paid him two hundred dirhams immediately and deferred two hundred dirhams to him, then her husband consummated the marriage with her, then her master subsequently sold her to another man. Whom do the deferred two hundred dirhams belong to, upon the husband?

He (peace be upon him) said: 'If the husband consummated the marriage with her while she was with him, and the master did not demand the remainder of the dowry from him until he sold her, then there is nothing for him [the master] upon him [the husband], nor for anyone else. And when the master sold her, she has become divorced from the free husband, if he knew this matter, for the sale of the slave woman is her divorce.'
ai.seo_question: What happens to the deferred dowry and the marital status when a master sells his slave wife to another man?
ai.summary: This ruling from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the legal mechanism of *talaq* (divorce) inherent in the sale of a slave woman, a concept rooted in the Prophet's tradition that 'her sale is her divorce.' It establishes that if the master sells the slave without explicitly claiming the deferred dowry from the free husband, the debt is extinguished, highlighting the interplay between property rights and marital status in Shia jurisprudence. The condition of the husband's knowledge ensures that the divorce is effective, reflecting the scholarly emphasis on clarity in legal transactions.
